categories.name: Client Issue
categories.description: Emails from clients reporting problems with placed staff, service quality, or expressing dissatisfaction that could lead to contract termination or loss of business.

categories.name: Action Required
categories.description: Emails that demand an immediate and specific action from the recipient, often with a deadline or consequence for inaction.

categories.name: Client Request
categories.description: Emails from clients requesting new placements, changes to existing placements, or information about services and billing.

categories.name: Applicant
categories.description: Emails from job seekers applying for positions or following up on their applications.

categories.name: Billing & Payments
categories.description: Emails related to invoices, payments received, or payment reminders.

categories.name: System Alert
categories.description: Automated notifications about account activity, security, or system changes that may require review but not necessarily immediate action.

categories.name: Vendor & Product Updates
categories.description: Emails from software vendors or service providers about product updates, new features, or trial expirations.

categories.name: Newsletter & Marketing
categories.description: Promotional emails, newsletters, and webinars that are informational but not directly related to ongoing client or applicant management.

questions: Should emails about job posting expirations (e.g., HireLoop Postings - Your job posting expires in 3 days) be considered 'Action Required' or a lower priority 'System Alert'?
Emails like 'Delivery Status Notification (Failure)' (e18) indicate a problem with an outgoing email. Should these be a separate category or grouped with 'System Alert'?

For emails from vendors like Payrollly Billing (e23) and Ledgerleaf Accounts (e29) that are invoices or past due notices, should these be a distinct 'Invoices' category, or are they well-placed in 'Billing & Payments'?
